title: How a counter wraps
modelNote: Each real counter tick adds one. This teaching counter keeps only {width} bits; the program below uses {realWidth}-bit registers. Its readings are unsigned: zero or positive.
instruction: Use +1 until the stored reading wraps to zero, then press −1. Watch Carry out change to Borrow needed. Keep counting in either direction.
initialNote: The dash means no addition or subtraction is shown yet.
forwardWrapped: The extra carry lies beyond the {width} stored bits. The stored bits wrap to zero.
backwardWrapped: Subtraction must borrow one group of {range} from the next position. Taking one leaves {stored} in {width} bits.
forwardNormal: The addition stays within the stored bits. Carry out is zero.
backwardNormal: The subtraction stays at or above zero. No borrow from beyond the stored bits is needed.
architectureNote: RISC-V has no carry or signed-overflow flag. The carry or borrow marker belongs to this four-bit model.
initialStatus: Stored reading: {stored}. No step is shown.
